do.rule: Maintain correct side-gripping of the gourd for all characters handling mate to preserve physical realism.
Maintain consistent side-grip illustration on gourd props.
Maintain consistent counter-to-character proportions across wide kitchen shots.
Illustrate explicit actions (cutting, grinding, smoking) described in process steps rather than relying on static standing characters.
Keep main figures centered away from vertical edge boundaries.
Ensure instructional verbs (shake, flip, tilt, pour) are directly animated rather than showing a static object.
Ensure all ground-level props such as crates, bags, and fires have proper shadow contacts to prevent floating.
Match physical instructional verbs (flipping, shaking, pouring) with dedicated object rotation and motion animations.
Ensure hands are physically interacting with objects by wrapping fingers around them rather than just placing them nearby.
Maintain clear separation between top caption bars and character head outlines.
When a specific tool or action (like a spoon or scraping motion) is named in the narration, ensure that specific hero object is drawn in the hand and animated.
Ensure literal visual actions directly depict key nouns and verbs spoken in the voiceover.
Keep informational charts and text pills well-aligned above or below key visual elements to maintain clarity.
Ensure background elements remain entirely inside camera viewport bounds.
Maintain consistent character positioning and grounding across sequential shots.

avoid.rule: Avoid repeating static character poses across consecutive frames without subtle movement
Avoid repeating identical multi-character framing across consecutive shots.
Avoid showing multiple mate gourds in sharing scenes where one shared mate is culturally appropriate.
Avoid vertical displacement or scaling jumps of characters between consecutive shots.
Avoid using the exact same generic indoor warehouse background across multiple distinct manufacturing stages.
Avoid text overlay desynchronization with audio transcript.
Avoid scaling prop models out of realistic proportions relative to character hands.
Do not repeat identical multi-character lineup frames consecutively without changing composition.
Avoid placing small background characters so low that their lower halves get clipped by the canvas frame.
Avoid placing text or labels directly over character faces to maintain clear expressions.
Avoid static visual repetitions across consecutive short shots to maintain visual interest.
Avoid showing isolated static props on tables when text explicitly describes active handling.
Avoid reusing identical character poses across too many sequential frames without a micro-action.
Avoid reusing particle animation loops across distinct spoken context changes.
Avoid exaggerated object scaling that distorts the physical logic of everyday items.
Do not repeat identical static object shots across consecutive dialogue lines without changing camera perspective or character action.
Avoid overlapping held hero objects directly on body centerlines without offset.
Never place graphic warning marks, text, or crosses over character faces.
Do not mix flat vector templates into pixel8 reels.
Avoid using generic placeholder geometry when specific object flaws are narrated.
